    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.
Både Timon Haugan og Henrik Kristoffersen tapte halvannet sekund til Braathen i første omgang. Begge fortsatte å skuffe i andre omgang og ble henholdsvis 18 og 19.
– Jeg kjørte i en stein, forteller Kristoffersen til TV 2.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Vind og kaos-skyting: Kirkeeide vant fellesstarten etter åtte (!) bom</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/vind-og-kaos-skyting_-kirkeeide-vant-fellesstarten-etter-atte-___-bom-1.18082184</link>
      <description>Maren Kirkeeide stakk av med seieren på kvinnenes fellesstart i skiskyting på Geilo søndag.
Lørdagens sprintsensasjon Guro Ytterhus imponerte igjen og tok andreplass 14,4 sekunder bak Kirkeeide.
Juni Arnekleiv ledet etter to fulle hus, men på tredje skyting ble det kaos. Sterk vind gjorde at flere av utøverne bommet mange ganger, og Arnekleiv røk på fire bom.
Dermed tok Karoline Knotten over teten. Men på siste skyting, så haglet skuddene utenfor blinkene nok en gang.
Og plutselig var Kirkeeide i tet etter hele åtte (!) bom. Få løpere måtte ut i flere strafferunder, men likevel holdt hun ledelsen helt til mål.
– Det var en merkelig fellesstart. Det var veldig mange som bommet. Det var tydeligvis ikke så lett som man skulle tro, sier Kirkeeide til NRK etter seieren.
Karoline Knotten tok tredjeplass.
Ingrid Landmark Tandrevold, Marthe Kråkstad Johansen, Karoline Knotten og nevnte Kirkeeide er forhåndsuttatt til verdenscupstarten i finske Kontiolahti senere i måneden. Kvinnenes tropp skal til slutt bestå av seks løpere.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/stor-oslo/kraftig-brann-i-lillestrom-1.18081998</link>
      <description>Det brenner kraftig i en enebolig på en gård i Trondheimsveien i Lillestrøm.
– Det er full fyr i hele bygningen, opplyser oppdragsleder i politiet, Ronny Mangseth.
– Brannvesenet er fremme og er i gang med slukking. Det er kontroll på alle fire beboere på stedet, sier han.
Ved 17:20-tiden opplyser politiet at det fortsatt brenner i boligen, og at arbeidet med slukking vil ta tid.
En person skal ha fått i seg noe røyk.
Det skal ikke være fare for spredning til låve eller andre bygninger på gården.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke kjent hva som er årsaken til brannen, og de vil etterforske saken videre.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Solbakken overrasker – Aasgaard inn i startelleveren</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/solbakken-overrasker-_-aasgaard-inn-i-startelleveren-1.18081988</link>
      <description>Ståle Solbakken har valgt ut følgende ellever til kampen mot Wales på Ullevaal:
Egil Selvik – Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Møller Wolfe – Sander Berge, Martin Ødegaard, Thelo Aasgaard – Antonio Nusa, Erling Braut Haaland, Oscar Bobb.
– Jeg må innrømme at jeg er noe overrasket. Men da tenker vel Solbakken at han passer bedre til denne kampen enn det Patrick Berg gjør akkurat nå, sier NRK-ekspert Andrine Hegerberg om at Aasgaards inntog i startelleveren.
Han er én av fire bytter som er gjort fra elleveren som møtte Portugal i forrige nasjonsligakamp.
Leo Østigård, Andreas Schjelderup og Patrick Berg er henvist til benken, mens Fredrik Aursnes ikke er med på grunn av en skade.
Samtidig er det nok en gang Egil Selvik som skal vokte buret for Norge.
– Jeg er først og fremst stolt, men også spent. Det blir en viktig kamp for oss, så det gjelder å gi jernet. Vi har noe å revansjere, sier Selvik til TV 2.
På motsatt banehalvdel starter Wales med følgende mannskap:
Karl Darlow – Neco Williams, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Jay Dasilva – Harry Wilson, Ethan Ampadu, Liam Cullen, Daniel James – Lewis Koumas, Brennan Johnson.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/britisk-politi-starter-etterforskning-av-david-walliams-1.18081553</link>
      <description>Britisk politi bekrefter overfor BBC at de har innledet en etterforskning mot komikeren David Walliams for alvorlige seksuelle forbrytelser.
Det skjer etter at flere kvinner har stått frem med anklager om at Walliams skal ha brukt kjendisstatusen sin for å tilnærme seg unge kvinner seksuelt.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke disse anklagene som er grunnlaget for etterforskningen.
Walliams er kjent for humorserien «Little Britain» og har de senere årene blant annet gjort seg bemerket som barnebokforfatter.
Han har avvist å ha gjort noe galt.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Thore «Henki» Holm Hansen er død</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/thore-_henki_-holm-hansen-er-dod-1.18081252</link>
      <description>Den tidligere Outlaws-sjefen og countrymusikeren er død, 82 år gammel, melder VG.
Holm Hansen ledet MC-klubben Outlaws, ble dømt for handel med narkotika og våpen og ga ut countrymusikk.
«Han sovnet stille inn på morgenen i dag, hjemme hos meg i sin egen seng, med venner og familie rundt seg», skriver datteren hans June Nordlie i et innlegg på Facebook.
Holm Hansen ble i 1981 dømt til 60 års fengsel i en kokainsak i USA, men ble besluttet deportert til Norge.
Selv hevdet han at dommen var et justismord, og knyttet saken til påstått arbeid for CIA.</description>

      <description>Microsoft opplever tekniske problemer som rammer brukere av blant annet e-posttjenesten Outlook og Teams. Selskapet opplyser at de jobber med å løse saken.
Også andre Microsoft-produkter er berørt, blant annet SharePoint og Planner.
Årsaken er at en del av infrastrukturen opplevde «forhøyet belastning, ifølge Microsoft. Selskapet fant ut at en rekke servere var «uventet utilgjengelige».
Ifølge nettstedet Downdetector nådde problemene et høydepunkt ved 19-tiden norsk tid, med 129 476 feilmeldinger.
Ved 5.30-tiden natt til fredag har antallet feilmeldinger falt til 21 988.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/skolebuss-av-veien-i-larvik-1.18079991</link>
      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.
– Bussen har sklidd av veien og ut i grøfta med alle fire hjul. I bussen er det 24 barn som fremstår uskadd, skriver operasjonsleder Per Magne Eftang i politiloggen.
Bussjåføren er også uskadd, ifølge politiet.
– Barna er nå på vei ut av bussen og inn et hus for å holde varmen, sier Eftang til NRK.
Han sier alle barna brukte bilbelte.
Operasjonslederen antar at hendelsen kan knyttes til det glatte føret, men politiet har ikke kommet fram til stedet ennå.
Klokka 09.44 opplyser politiet at ingen er skadet. Flere foreldre har hentet barna sine og ny buss er klar til å frakte resten av barna til skolen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ Independent and employee owned - local news stories, weather, sports, events and more Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:44:28 +0000 en-CA hourly 1 https://cheknews.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/cropped-CHEK-Mark-512x512-1-200x200.png?crop=1 CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ 32 32 70014466 Robert Pattinson is named the 7th James Bond, taking over the role from Daniel Craig https://cheknews.ca/robert-pattinson-is-named-the-7th-james-bond-taking-over-the-role-from-daniel-craig-1361600/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:16:52 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361600

Robert Pattinson was unveiled as the next James Bond on Monday, becoming the seventh actor to play the iconic British spy and the first since Amazon MGM took over the beloved film franchise.

The post Robert Pattinson is named the 7th James Bond, taking over the role from Daniel Craig appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Robert Pattinson was unveiled as the next James Bond on Monday, becoming the seventh actor to play the iconic British spy and the first since Amazon MGM took over the beloved film franchise.

The naming of Pattinson comes during the longest hiatus in 007 history and ends years of rampant speculation about who would inherit the role from Daniel Craig. It comes five years after 2021’s “No Time to Die,” the first film in Bond’s 64-year history on the silver screen to conclude with the character’s death. But 007 will be reborn, yet again, in the 26th Bond film, directed by Denis Villeneuve.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “… To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Pattinson only entered the Bond rumor mill recently after the revelation that he screen-tested for the role. Others reportedly in the mix included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult.

While producers were long expected to go with a young, less-proven star, they instead opted for one of the best-known actors of his generation. Pattinson, 40, is also relatively old to begin as 007. The actor is currently in production on another iconic role in “The Batman Part II.”

Pattinson comes in already associated with three mega-franchises in “The Batman,” “Twilight” and “Harry Potter.” But since his breakthrough in “Twilight,” Pattinson has worked largely in more independent, auteur-driven films such as “Good Time” with the Safdie brothers, Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse” and Bong Joon Ho’s “Mickey 17.” Earlier this year, he drew rave reviews for his villainous performance in Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey.”

The casting comes at a pivotal juncture for the franchise. In 2022, Bond’s longtime studio, MGM, was bought by Amazon for $8.5 billion. After haggling over next steps for 007, producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson relinquished creative control of Bond in 2025. The still-untitled Bond 26 is the first Bond movie since 1962’s inaugural “Dr. No” where a Broccoli didn’t handpick the super spy.

Casting a new Bond fell instead to producers Amy Pascal — the former Sony Pictures chief and “Spider-Man” producer — and David Heyman, shepherd of “Harry Potter” and “Paddington.” Steven Knight (“Peaky Blinders,” “Locke”) was brought in to write the script.

Before Craig even departed the role, rumors and odds-making persisted nearly round-the-clock on who would follow in the footsteps of Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Craig. Idris Elba, for one, has spent half his career deflecting 007 conjecture.

The Bond machine has historically never slowed down. But the 26th installment will follow the longest absence ever for Bond. Given that “No Time to Die” completed principal photography in 2019 (its release was delayed due to the coronavirus pandemic), the lull is even longer.

Some fans are skeptical about the new Amazon-controlled chapter for Bond. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, has vowed to uphold the franchise’s legacy and usher in “the next phase in the legendary 007 for audiences around the world.”

At stake is one of the most lucrative film series in Hollywood, based on Ian Fleming’s series of novels. The Bond movies have grossed more than $7 billion worldwide in ticket sales. “No Time to Die” collected $774 million in 2021. The movies also spin out endless other revenue streams, from streaming deals and video games to Aston Martins.

Although some Bond actors came to view the role as a yoke around their necks, it turned Craig into a household name. The British actor wasn’t widely known before his casting and, at the time, was derided as the first “blond Bond.”

]]> 1361600 Carney heads to China to meet with President Xi, leaders from across Pacific Rim https://cheknews.ca/carney-heads-to-china-to-meet-with-president-xi-leaders-from-across-pacific-rim-1361595/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:45:58 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361595

]]>

Prime Minister Mark Carney is travelling to China today, where he is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and leaders from across the Pacific Rim.

Carney is leaving the Francophonie summit in Cambodia and travelling to Shenzhen, China’s tech hub, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation summit.

He is scheduled to meet with Xi at a time that will be Tuesday morning in China but late Monday evening in Ottawa. Carney said Canada could do more with China in terms of agriculture, clean and conventional energy, and financial services.

“We’ve established pretty clear guardrails on the areas that we’re going to focus on … I’m using our words, not theirs,” he told reporters in Phnom Penh.

Carney also expects to speak with Xi about “the evolution of the international system, China’s role in that and Canadian priorities.”

An overarching topic will be Chinese investments into Canada’s auto sector. Both countries agreed earlier this year to allow a limited amount of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada.

Carney has said he wants Chinese carmakers to set up shop, but only if they provide decent jobs, saying he is wary of plants where workers assemble cars using components mostly made in China.

He said trade talks with Washington will shape how Canada approaches Chinese investment.

“It’s part of the trade negotiations,” he said. “Depending (on) where that settles, there’ll be other options — European options, Asian options.”

“This is not leverage, but you know, action-reaction. It depends.”

Carney will also meet with various leaders from the APEC forum, a group of 21 economies on both sides of the Pacific that work together to break down trade barriers. The grouping includes members as varied as Taiwan, Australia and Peru.

Carney’s office says he will stick with his focus of drumming up more investment and diversifying Canadian trade.

Vina Nadjibulla, co-founder of the Centre for Strategic Statecraft, said she’ll be watching to see whether Carney allows more Chinese investments into Canada “in critical sectors, in energy and technology, particularly related to renewables and batteries” in addition to auto manufacturing.

“We have to constantly triangulate our relationship with China with our discussions with the U.S. — and also watch then what happens between the U.S. and China bilaterally,” she said.

Nadjibulla also said the summit should help craft the foreign policy review that Carney aims to table in the House of Commons in the coming weeks, as well as next year’s planned renewal of the 2022 Indo-Pacific strategy launched by his predecessor Justin Trudeau. 

“We now have a really solid foundation,” Nadjibulla said, noting that leaders from Asia have visited Canada or are planning to, notably Vietnam and India.

“Canada is finally on their radar and has relevance to their own diversification agendas and their own economic security and resilience agendas.”

She said any update to Ottawa’s regional strategy must include a look at relations with Taiwan, a self-governing island which China claims. The federal cabinet has left a trade arrangement sitting unsigned for more than a year, despite the House foreign-affairs committee urging that government proceed with more economic relations.

During the APEC summit, U.S. President Donald Trump is set to meet President Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

That has raised alarm among European officials, as some suggest U.S.-brokered peace talks between Russia and Ukraine have included proposals they say would leave both Ukraine and Europe vulnerable.

Carney said Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva recently told him that he encouraged the talks in order to end the war. Carney said Canada wants a just peace for Ukraine and a ceasefire is needed.

Nadjibulla said it’s incredible the trilateral meeting might happen, adding that it reinforces Carney’s warnings about “unconstrained great-power politics” in his January speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos.

“It’s a reminder that other countries need to double down on their efforts to build resilience and agency, so that they don’t become collateral — so they don’t end up on the menu of great-power competition, but rather have a seat at the table,” she said.

China has indicated great enthusiasm for Carney’s visit. The state-controlled English-language newspaper Global Times has framed it as a mutually beneficial partnership in a turbulent world.

“The ability of China and Canada to address previous trade frictions through calm and equal-footed dialogue not only helps strengthen bilateral strategic mutual trust, but also injects confidence into global economic and trade co-operation,” said Zhao Xingshu of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, according to the newspaper.

“Nearly eight years of limited high-level exchanges mean rebuilding mutual understanding between officials and institutions will require time. At this stage, maintaining the momentum of stabilization in bilateral relations is itself an important and realistic objective.”

The APEC summit takes place in Shenzhen, which borders Hong Kong, where Canada has repeatedly expressed concern about growing repression as the territory transitions from semi-autonomy to full Chinese rule.

Earlier this month, Canada joined western peers in condemning 10-year sentences for politicians and democracy activists under national-security laws, particularly Joshua Wong.

“We call for an immediate end to all unjust prosecutions of individuals charged under the (national security law),” the joint statement says.

It urges Chinese leaders to “uphold their international commitments and honour the rights and freedoms guaranteed to the people of Hong Kong” when the British government ceded sovereignty.

Carney has said he raises human rights issues privately with China but avoids public criticism.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 16, 2026.

]]> 1361595 Inflation unchanged at 3.1% in October: StatCan https://cheknews.ca/inflation-unchanged-at-3-1-in-october-statcan-1361592/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:22:35 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361592

The annual rate of inflation remained steady at 3.1 per cent in October as higher prices for gas, groceries and clothes were subdued by cheaper cell phone plans and slower rent price growth, Statistics Canada said Monday.

The post Inflation unchanged at 3.1% in October: StatCan appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The annual rate of inflation remained steady at 3.1 per cent in October as higher prices for gas, groceries and clothes were subdued by cheaper cellphone plans and slower rent price growth, Statistics Canada said Monday.

The inflation rate came in slightly below economists’ expectations of 3.2 per cent.

Gasoline continued to be a key driver of headline inflation, rising 30.9 per cent year-over-year in October compared with 27.8 per cent the month before amid continued conflict in the Middle East and Ukraine.

Higher energy costs could eventually push up prices elsewhere, said Royal Bank of Canada economist Abbey Xu.

“The longer energy prices remain elevated, the more cost pressures will filter through to consumer prices with a lag,” she said in a client note. 

“The path of energy prices also remains highly uncertain despite the decline in gasoline prices so far in November.”

StatCan said gasoline prices rose at a faster annual pace last month partly due to a drop in crude oil prices in October 2025.

On a monthly basis, however, gasoline prices fell 2.5 per cent in October.

Excluding energy, annual inflation eased to two per cent in October from 2.1 per cent in September.

“Underlying price pressures stayed comparatively contained,” Xu said, noting that the consumer price index excluding both food and energy slowed to 1.8 per cent.

RBC’s diffusion index, which measures how widespread inflation is across the economy, continued to show that “unusually strong price growth has been concentrated in a relatively narrow share of the consumer basket,” she said. 

Meanwhile, Canadians once again faced higher prices at grocery stores.

StatCan said the cost of food purchased from stores accelerated to two per cent year-over-year in October after four consecutive months of slower price growth.

Fresh vegetable prices rose 1.4 per cent in October after falling 2.9 per cent in September while condiments, spices and vinegars were up 2.6 per cent.

Compared with October 2020, the agency said grocery prices have climbed 31.9 per cent.

Prices for clothing were up 1.8 per cent in October, driven by a 2.2 per cent year-over-year increase in women’s clothing and a 1.4 per cent increase in men’s clothing.

Clothing prices were up 3.4 per cent month-over-month in October, the largest monthly increase since September 2019.

StatCan said the price increases coincided with higher shipping costs.

In Ontario, prices for natural gas rose three per cent year-over-year in October after declining 18.7 per cent in September.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 16, 2026.

]]> 1361555 Island film production company takes aim at vertical filmmaking https://cheknews.ca/island-film-production-company-takes-aim-at-on-vertical-filmmaking-1361523/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 01:17:45 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361523

]]>

A newly created Vancouver Island film company is focusing on vertical storytelling formats, a growing global trend in how viewers consume film and TV.

It’s difficult to miss while scrolling on social media. Short, bite-sized episodes, often with a romantic or dramatic theme, and end with cliffhangers.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

These “microdramas” are produced entirely for viewers to consume through their phones.

“The vertical format is now becoming bigger than just the microdrama format. It’s growing into horror and other genres,” said Shera Skinner.

Skinner is a producer for NineSixteen Entertainment, a newly formed Vancouver Island-based film production company focusing solely on creating vertical films.

The company is now part of a new growing trend in storytelling in Canada. Vertical filming initially gained success in Asia during the pandemic and slowly made waves in North America, securing the attention of big-name actors like James Franco, who starred in a microdrama in the summer.

“Verticals are very quick; you get the information right away, it’s in your face, it’s louder…I think that’s basically the thing that will stick around is that the phones aren’t going anywhere,” said Jackie Taylor, director at NineSixteen Entertainment.

Despite the content being tailored for phones, Taylor says phones aren’t typically used for filming. Vertical production crews remain similar to traditional crews and so do the challenges of creating a film, but Taylor says costs can often be lower.

“Less crew, you definitely have less time to shoot a movie the same size as a regular feature,” said Taylor.

“The pace is a lot of faster, you get two takes or one and done,” said Skinner.

Globally, it’s estimated that microdramas brought in $11 billion USD in revenue in 2025, and the industry could be worth $30 billion USD by 2030.

Canadian filmmakers and actors say it’s a growing trend. A vertical film made its debut at a Newfoundland film festival last week, and now the CBC is taking aim at short-form content under 15 minutes.

Skinner has starred in at least eight vertical films, but because all were in Vancouver, that led her, Taylor, and others to launch NineSixteen.

“We’re among the very first…we see all the people that have this skill and they’re ready to make the stories…I’m kind of sick of taking the ferry. There is no reason we can’t make this product on the Island.”

Much of the work in vertical filmmaking is non-unionized, but Skinner thinks that could change because she says unions are interested in being involved with the new format.

“Some of the bigger production companies are starting to use unions and there is a subsection of the collective agreement for the actors unions, to use for vertical productions,”

One union,  IATSE 891, even became a gold sponsor for the first Canadian Vertical Film Festival (CVFF), which was founded by Taylor and Chris Chisholm. CVFF was held earlier this summer at the Victoria International Marina and had more than 30 submissions.

“Go for vertical, make a short film that’s a vertical,” said Taylor.

NineSixteen Entertainment is taking its first shot at a horror vertical film, It Wants Inside, which follows a young woman whose life takes a terrifying turn after an evening with friends and a mysterious spirit board.

A Kickstarter for the film has been launched and the company aims to being production next month.

Lacing up and getting ready to run, two fourth-year University of Victoria students are right at home on the track.

“Running’s kind of just always been a part of my life,” Kai Dorin says.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“I did track and cross country in high school, and I’ve done a lot of the Vancouver Island Race series, so 8Ks, 10Ks, and then my favourite is the 5K,” adds Nicholas Sakamoto.

But Nicholas Sakamoto and Kai Dorin are now training for their most epic — and most daunting — run yet.

“This year I think there’s going to be a huge mental aspect trying to run for 24 hours in circles, basically,” Nicholas explains.

He’s not exaggerating. On Nov. 29, the duo will be running for 24 hours straight around the Oak Bay track to raise money and awareness for men’s health.

“Fundraising for Movember is super important to us,” Kai says. “I think mental health is is something that’s really overlooked. I think there’s a large stigma on men’s health, specifically.”

“About three-quarters of suicides are men, which is really unfortunate,” Nicholas adds. “And especially nowadays with the social media landscape, there’s a lot of stigma and kind of encouragement to bottle up emotions, and we’re just trying to do our best to reduce that.”

This will be their second big Movember fundraiser, after pounding the pavement from Victoria to Nanaimo last year.

“It was certainly towards the 70 to 80-kilometer mark, that’s when when things got pretty dark out and and in our minds, too,” Kai admits.

But the pair pushed through the pain, and the rain, raising more than $8,500 and winning the Movember ‘Going the Distance’ award.

“It was pretty awesome,” Nicholas says. “It was a very surreal moment.”

“While it was nice to be recognized, that was never our goal,” Kai adds. “Our goal is to raise money for for a cause.”

They’re hoping to keep the momentum going this year. but they know circling the track for 24 hours won’t be easy.

“Lots of gels, lots of caffeine,” Nicholas says. “We had some sushi last year that worked out pretty well, so maybe we’ll have some sushi in the middle there. And yeah, lots of hydration, lots of Gatorade and stuff like that.”

“I think we’ll have a lot of support, especially in the in the daylight but once nighttime comes around, it it’s just it’ll just be Nick and I in the dark so that’s when the mental will really take control of us,” Nick says.

But running has always been what’s helped these friends get through tough times and go the distance.

“Especially through COVID, I used it as kind of an outlet where I could just relax and not worry about things,” Nicholas says.

“Running kind of helps me calm down,” says Kai. “It it helped me in some pretty dark moments in my life.”

You could have expected the mood around the Mungo Martin Big House in Victoria to be somber Sunday as people gathered to talk about James “Dakota” Smith.

He’s an Indigenous man who has been missing north of Sayward for over a week, but there was more hope than sadness.

“We are very hopeful, we are still looking for him,” Dakota Smith’s aunt Edith Louie told CHEK News.

Watch the report below:

Loading the player...

Smith is a husband and father of two who recently moved to the ancestral land of the Ma-amtagila people near the mouth of the Adam River north of Sayward.

On Friday, Nov. 6 he went out in his canoe to dispose of an elk carcass but might have got caught in a storm because his empty canoe was later found about 11 kilometres to the west on the other side of the Johnstone Strait.

There are now new details about why he might have been eager to dispose of those bones even in the face of inclement weather.

“Dakota had said grizzly bears were coming closer to his home so he thought he would clean up their area,” family supporter Rose Henry said.

Family members say Smith had set up several caches with survival gear in the area in case someone came across it and needed it.

Now they hope he’s still hunkered down with one somewhere, alive.

“Our people continue to search until there’s proof of one or the other,” Louie added.

“Our people, we never give up. We’ve heard rumours, you know, let it go, he’s passed away. I said I’ve heard those rumours before,” Henry said. “I said I heard it when Bear went missing, I never give up.”

She’s speaking about her nephew Bear Henry, who was missing for over two months in November 2021 before being found alive by loggers near Fairy Creek.

“And so I hold that same hope that this is going to happen with Dakota too,” said Henry.

The community-led search north of Sayward refocused on the water last week.

The group is still seeking financial help to pay for boats and helicopters.

“He was the type of person who if you needed something, you ask him and good chances he was going to say yes right away,” said Henry.

]]> 1361519 Victoria’s St. Margaret’s School receives $22M donation for campus upgrades, wellness centre https://cheknews.ca/victorias-st-margarets-school-receives-22m-donation-for-campus-upgrades-wellness-centre-1361503/ Sun, 15 Nov 2026 23:08:12 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361503

A private girls’ school in Victoria has received a $22-million donation that will fund major campus improvements, including the construction of a new Health and Wellness Centre.

St. Margaret’s School announced the gift in a news release, describing it as a significant investment in the school’s future as it approaches its 120th anniversary.

The funding will support the school’s 2025-2030 strategic plan, which focuses on student wellbeing, academic development, leadership and improvements to campus facilities.

At the centre of the project is a new Health and Wellness Centre designed to support the physical, emotional, social and academic wellbeing of students and staff.

“Parents want their daughters to be successful,” said Sara Blair, CEO and head of St. Margaret’s School.

“But more than that, they want them to know who they are, believe in what they can become, and have the confidence to shape the future.”

Founded in 1908, St. Margaret’s is the oldest continuously operating independent school on Vancouver Island, offering day and boarding education for girls.
